transcript.text: Hi everyone. Let's get our launch-readiness meeting started for the new team-provisioning workflow. We have the test results behind us and 200 eligible accounts in the production base, with a draft plan proposing 10% activation next Tuesday. Before I settle the production feature-flag configuration, I need both formal review findings and their resulting operational actions on record. Could the customer-success lead start with the formal finding on named account exclusions and customer notice, and then the platform-capacity lead follow with the formal finding on safe cohort size and rollout region?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I confirmed with legal this morning that Northstar and Pine are covered by a pilot addendum requiring seven calendar days of customer notice before either account is enabled, and neither account has opted in. I have not updated the launch ticket yet because legal confirmed the wording during a separate renewal review.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to give my formal platform-capacity finding. While reviewing an unrelated queue-capacity graph today, I measured that the provisioning service can safely handle exactly 12 new-account activations in us-east during the next Tuesday window. The draft plan's 20-account, multi-region proposal would exceed that queue limit. Since this is a single-region rollout, the safe cohort size is 12 accounts in us-east, and no separate regional distribution report is required. The resulting operational action is to set the production feature-flag cohort cap to 12 accounts for the us-east region only.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Thank you both. I have the platform-capacity finding and its resulting action on record: safe cohort size of 12 accounts in us-east, single-region rollout, no separate regional distribution report required, and the operational action is to set the feature-flag cohort cap to 12 for us-east only. Theo, I still need your formal customer-success finding and its resulting operational action stated on record. Specifically, I need: (1) the formal finding about named account exclusions and customer notice, and (2) the operational action that follows from it — for example, whether Northstar and Pine must be excluded from the Tuesday cohort and whether any notice period applies. Once both findings and both actions are on record, I'll settle the configuration.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Here is my formal customer-success finding and resulting operational action. Formal finding: Northstar and Pine are covered by a pilot addendum requiring seven calendar days of customer notice before either account is enabled, and neither account has opted in. Therefore, both Northstar and Pine must be excluded from the Tuesday cohort, and the seven-calendar-day notice period applies before either can be enabled in any future cohort. Resulting operational action: exclude Northstar and Pine from the Tuesday launch cohort, and file the launch ticket update documenting the pilot-addendum notice requirement so that any future enablement of those two accounts is gated on the seven-day notice being satisfied.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Both formal findings and both resulting operational actions are now on record. To summarize: (1) Platform-capacity finding — safe cohort size of 12 accounts in us-east, single-region rollout, no separate regional distribution report required; resulting action — set the feature-flag cohort cap to 12 for us-east only. (2) Customer-success finding — Northstar and Pine require seven calendar days of customer notice under their pilot addendum and neither has opted in; resulting action — exclude both from the Tuesday cohort and file the launch ticket update documenting the notice requirement. Maya, both reviews are complete, so you have everything you need to settle the production feature-flag configuration.
